title: How do eight decimal patterns go on?
description: Eight patterns of decimals are shown, five rising and three falling. The change is found by taking each term from the next, added for a rising pattern and taken away for a falling one. Keeko's doubt adds the change to a falling pattern.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rising pattern keeps adding its change and a falling pattern keeps taking it away. Watch for students who always add the change.

source: Find the change and the next 3 terms: (a) 4.4, 4.45, 4.5 (b)
video_script.why: The child has continued one rising pattern and now meets patterns that fall, and changes of different sizes.
video_script.substitution: Take each term from the next to get the change, then add it if the numbers rise and take it away if they fall.
video_script.anchor: Eight patterns of decimal numbers on the board, each with three terms shown.
video_script.wrong_move: Adds the change to a falling pattern, so the next term is higher than the last instead of lower.
video_script.payoff_line: When the numbers fall, the change is taken away

final_answer.spoken: the first goes on with four point five five, four point six zero and four point six five; the second with twenty seven point two five, twenty seven point seven five and twenty eight point two five; the third with ten point eight nine, eleven and eleven point one one; the fourth with twenty one, twenty three point five and twenty six; the fifth with eleven point two, twelve point one and thirteen; the sixth with four point eight five, four point eight zero and four point seven five; the seventh with ten point nine five, ten point four five and nine point nine five; the last with twenty six, twenty two point five and nineteen

maths_rules: the slip: in (f), 4.90 + 0.05 = 4.95 is higher than 4.90, but the pattern falls
video_script.design: Eight number rows stay on the board, each with a jump arrow between neighbours. Rising rows get arrows pointing up and falling rows get arrows pointing down, and three new boxes fill in one row at a time.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the change in each, and what are the next three numbers?

narration: <bookmark mark='term'/>Each number in a pattern is called a term.
<bookmark mark='change'/>The change is what we add or take away to get from one term to the next.
<bookmark mark='dir'/>If the terms rise, we add the change. If they fall, we take it away.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, take each term away from the next term.
<bookmark mark='rise'/>The first five patterns rise.
<bookmark mark='c1'/>Their changes are zero point zero five, zero point five and zero point one one.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Then two point five and zero point nine.
<bookmark mark='fall'/>The last three patterns fall.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>Their changes are zero point zero five, zero point five and three point five.

beats.on_screen: rising rows: add the change to the last term; (c) 10.78 + 0.11 = 10.89, then 10.89 + 0.11 = 11.00, then 11.00 + 0.11 = 11.11

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, in a rising pattern, add the change to the last term.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Take the third pattern. Ten point seven eight plus zero point one one is ten point eight nine.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Keep adding to get the next two terms.

beats.on_screen: falling rows: take the change away from the last term; (h) 29.5 - 3.5 = 26.0, then 26.0 - 3.5 = 22.5, then 22.5 - 3.5 = 19.0

marks.rule: the words take the change away are written beside the falling rows
marks.ex: 29.5 - 3.5 = 26.0 is written for the last row
marks.keep: the next two terms of the last row fill in, and the other falling rows fill in the same way

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, in a falling pattern, take the change away from the last term.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Take the last pattern. Twenty nine point five take away three point five is twenty six.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Keep taking away to get the next two terms.

narration: <bookmark mark='look'/>Keeko looks at five, four point nine five, four point nine zero.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>Keeko thinks the next term is four point nine five, adding the change.
<bookmark mark='higher'/>But four point nine five is higher than four point nine zero, and this pattern is falling.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A falling pattern needs the change taken away, so the next term is four point eight five.
